controlTower.intro: Design owner of the Agent Control Tower at OOCL — a multi-service platform centered on a warm agent pool for high-volume agent tasks, with a generic agent platform on top: knowledge space, self-improvement pipeline, dynamic workflow, active notification system, dynamic dashboard, agent registry, human-in-the-loop approval, live state tracking, and spec versioning. Every action is attributable; every change is versioned.
controlTower.openSource: aria-conductor is the open-source simplification: Java 21 and React, approval gates, agent chains, and a concurrency harness.
controlTower.note: Validated end-to-end on a Docker/Podman compose stack — operator UI, core services, MySQL and MongoDB. An always-available registry/forwarder removed a startup failure where A2A card fetch blocked worker boot; dispatch now fails fast instead of blocking.

decomposer.body: Designed the job-decomposer library in the platform scheduler. A job is decomposed recursively into tasks and sub-tasks across N levels, then dispatched over asynchronous messaging. The heartbeat loop keeps dispatching, respects queue limits, and applies backpressure so large or continuously loaded jobs do not stall. Workers scale from configuration or available resources; job definitions persist in the scheduler and dispatch through its processing API.

observability.body: Production observability on Rancher-managed Kubernetes. I own the metrics, logs, cloud monitoring, and release checks for a 20+ service platform, and use the same signals to verify rollouts and investigate incidents.

projects.name: aria-conductor
projects.description: Java 21 + React 19 control tower for agent chains. Fixed a concurrent-approval race that allowed double approvals; built the load and concurrency harness.
projects.cvDescription: Designed and built a multi-service control tower: Java 21/Spring Boot backend, React 19/TypeScript dashboard, Node/TypeScript MCP server, MariaDB/H2, Docker/Podman, and per-agent OpenSandbox containers. Implemented governance and operator workflows: task approval gates, versioned knowledge, BA→Dev→QA agent chains, live run status, kanban, and activity timeline. Fixed a concurrent-approval race where two opposing approvals could both pass the same pending check and commit; replaced read-check-write with an atomic conditional update, so one request wins and the other is rejected with an HTTP 409 conflict. Fixed a 500 that rolled back the whole transaction under mixed load; built the load and concurrency E2E harness plus Playwright UI coverage.
